fixes.explanation: Ararat it is. "On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat." (Genesis 8:4) After all that floating, the ark finally comes to rest. I bet that felt like good news on board.

Mountains! "…on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible." (Genesis 8:5) The waters kept receding until the tenth month, and now the tops of the mountains show. After years in the back of a junk drawer, I know how good it feels when something new finally comes into view. I bet Noah looked at that view for a good long while.

True. Noah sent out a raven, and "It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth." (Genesis 8:7) Back and forth, back and forth, that raven had a whole route going. I'm tired just picturing it. I think that bird earned a long nap.

That's true, friend. Genesis 8:7 says Noah "…sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth." The raven keeps going back and forth right up until the waters had dried up. Nothing in the verse says it stopped sooner.

Dry! "…Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry." (Genesis 8:13) The waters had dried up from the earth. I bet that was a sight after all that water. I'd have stared at that ground like it was a fresh batch coming out of the oven.

The clean ones. "…taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar." (Genesis 8:20) Right after Noah comes out of the ark, he builds an altar to the LORD. Of everything he could have done first, that's what the text shows him doing. I think that tells you where his heart was.

True. The LORD says in His heart, "Never again will I curse the ground because of man…" (Genesis 8:21) He says it right after Noah's offering, and He says it even though "…every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth." A promise like that is worth holding onto.

That's true, friend. The LORD says in His heart, "Never again will I curse the ground because of man…" (Genesis 8:21) He says it even though "…every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth." That promise is right there in the text, word for word.

Right. What the LORD says in His heart is, "And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done." (Genesis 8:21) That's the opposite of someday doing it again. He says it once more when He makes His covenant: "…never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth." (Genesis 9:11)

His rainbow! God says, "I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth." (Genesis 9:13) He calls it His rainbow, and He sets it in the clouds. Next time you spot one, you'll know what it's a sign of.

He remembers His covenant. God says, "I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of every kind." (Genesis 9:15) Then in the next verse He adds, "…I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant…" (Genesis 9:16). That's a promise with a sign hung up in the sky, and I like a promise I can look up and see. Whenever clouds form and that rainbow shows, you know what it's about.
